get.summary: One automation, its rule and its audit trail.

patch.summary: Changes an automation. Answers 409 when expectedUpdatedAt does not match, so an edit on a phone cannot silently overwrite one made on a tablet.

delete.summary: Deletes an automation. Idempotent: a second call answers 200 with the same body, never 404.

patch.summary: Activates, pauses, disables or drafts an automation, and reports how many pending runs were cancelled.

get.summary: Who created, changed, activated, paused or deleted it, and when.

How the caller's automations have been behaving: executions, success rate, failure breakdown, durations, dead letters and the actions that fail most. Owner-scoped exactly as the history is — no owner parameter, and an automation the caller may not read answers 404 rather than a denial.
One run, with what each condition decided and what each action produced.

post.summary: Runs a manual automation. Refuses an event-driven one: a client must not be able to manufacture a trigger.
A dry run against real state. Nothing is sent, nothing is charged and nobody is notified — enforced at the dispatcher, not by a flag.
How many people an automation would reach, as a count and a sentence. Never a member list, and small counts are banded.

get.summary: What this member may do. Self only; there is no read-another-member's-capabilities variant.

What a trigger would be checked against for one subject, so a member can see a rule will match before they save it. Public fields and non-sensitive condition values only, and it says plainly when a subject cannot be described.

delete.summary: Deletes a saved search. Idempotent.
